definitionEn: calm, serious behaviour that makes people respect you, especially in a difficult situation
senseNote: Здесь — про спокойное, достойное поведение человека в трудной ситуации. Более широкое значение «человеческое достоинство» (human dignity, права человека) в упражнениях не используется.
situation: Someone stays calm and self-respecting while going through a painful, embarrassing or unfair experience.

examples.text: She lost her job without warning but handled the situation with remarkable [[dignity]].
The manager criticised him in front of everyone, yet he kept his [[dignity]] throughout the meeting.
The company's former CEO responded to the scandal with quiet [[dignity]], never once blaming his colleagues.

texts: Her speech was short but full of quiet [[dignity]].
The old teacher retired with great [[dignity]] after forty years of service.
Even in poverty, the family kept its [[dignity]].

badCollocation.text: He remained calm and [[dignity]] during the whole trial.
badCollocation.noteRu: После calm and нужно прилагательное: dignified. Dignity — существительное, в этой позиции не используется.

collocationTask.prompt: Everyone should have the right to die with ___.
collocationTask.explanationRu: Die with dignity — уйти из жизни достойно, сохранив самоуважение. Die in peace и die comfortably — устойчивые обороты с другой структурой, die with peace/comfort/ease так не говорят.

nuance.text: She lost the election but left the stage with quiet [[dignity]].
nuance.explanationRu: Dignity — как человек сам держится в трудной ситуации; respect — то, как к нему относятся другие. Здесь важно её поведение, а не чужая оценка.

reverse.text: Great players always show [[respect]] for their opponents.
reverse.explanationRu: Уважение к другим людям — respect. Dignity — про собственное достойное поведение, а не отношение к кому-то ещё.

fixIt.text: After losing the case, the lawyer accepted the verdict with quiet [[politeness]].
fixIt.explanationRu: Вежливость (politeness) — не главное здесь. Достойно принять решение суда, сохранив самоуважение, — with dignity.

wordFormation.text: Even in the hospital bed, he looked calm and [[dignified]].

reply.context: A friend says: "I can't believe they made him clean out his desk in front of everyone."
options: I know, but he handled it with real dignity — he just packed up and left.
I know, he's always had so much dignity, that's probably why he got promoted twice.
Indeed, his conduct exhibited an exemplary degree of dignity befitting the occasion.
reply.explanationRu: Dignity — сохранять самоуважение и спокойствие в трудной ситуации, это и есть уместный ответ. Второй вариант связывает dignity с карьерным успехом — не то значение. Третий — слишком официально для разговора с другом.

definitionEn: a difficult situation that forces you to choose between two important but conflicting options
senseNote: Более простой уровень CEFR-J, вероятно, о бытовом использовании (какой цвет выбрать). Здесь — серьёзная, часто этическая дилемма, требующая взвешенного решения.
situation: A person or organisation must choose between two options, and neither of them is clearly the right one.

examples.text: Doctors sometimes face an ethical [[dilemma]] when a patient refuses life-saving treatment.
The journalist faced a moral [[dilemma]]: publish the leaked documents or protect her source.
Choosing between two excellent job offers is a nice [[dilemma]] to have.

texts: Every parent faces this [[dilemma]] at some point.
The committee found itself in a real [[dilemma]] over the budget cuts.
It's a classic [[dilemma]]: save money now or invest in the future.

badCollocation.text: I have a [[dilemma]] about which colour to paint the fence.
badCollocation.noteRu: Dilemma — выбор между двумя вариантами, когда оба по-своему сложны или важны. Для простого бытового выбора говорят question или decision, а не dilemma.

collocationTask.prompt: She was on the horns of a ___, unable to choose between the two candidates.
collocationTask.explanationRu: On the horns of a dilemma — идиома «оказаться перед трудным выбором». Fence, edge и fork с horns of a ___ не сочетаются, это не устойчивое выражение.

nuance.text: Deciding which parent to live with after the divorce was a heartbreaking [[dilemma]] for the teenager.
nuance.explanationRu: Dilemma — трудный выбор между двумя вариантами, часто оба тяжелы эмоционально. Problem — просто трудность, без обязательного выбора между двумя сторонами.

reverse.text: The photocopier keeps breaking down — it's becoming a real [[problem]] in the office.
reverse.explanationRu: Постоянная поломка — это problem (техническая неполадка), а не dilemma: тут не нужно выбирать между двумя вариантами.

fixIt.text: The company faced a difficult [[problem]]: raise prices or cut jobs to survive the crisis.
fixIt.explanationRu: Выбор между двумя болезненными вариантами (поднять цены или сократить штат) — это dilemma, а не просто problem.

reply.context: A friend texts: "I got offered two amazing jobs on the same day and I have to answer both by Friday!"
options: What a dilemma! Both sound great, so at least you can't really lose.
Yeah, waking up with a headache this morning was such a dilemma.
Who cares, just flip a coin and stop bothering me about it.
reply.explanationRu: Dilemma — выбор между двумя вариантами; головная боль — это не dilemma, а просто problem. Третий ответ звучит грубо для сообщения другу.

rewrite.original: She couldn't decide whether to stay in her hometown or move abroad for the job.
rewrite.frame: She faced a real ____ about whether to stay or move abroad.
rewrite.explanationRu: Трудный выбор между двумя вариантами — dilemma.

definitionEn: an aspect of a situation, problem or plan that is important to think about
senseNote: Базовое значение — физическое измерение (длина, ширина, высота: the dimensions of a room). Здесь — переносное: сторона, аспект ситуации или проблемы.
situation: A writer, speaker or thinker points out another important aspect of a complicated problem or situation.

examples.text: The scandal added a political [[dimension]] to what had been a purely financial story.
Her research explores the emotional [[dimension]] of long-distance relationships.
Climate change adds a worrying new [[dimension]] to global food security.

texts: There's also a legal [[dimension]] to consider.
The story has a surprising human [[dimension]] that most reports ignore.
Every negotiation has an emotional [[dimension]] as well as a financial one.

badCollocation.text: Can you tell me the [[dimension]] of the table?
badCollocation.noteRu: Про размеры физического предмета говорят dimensions во множественном числе: the dimensions of the table. Dimension в единственном числе — это скорее «сторона, аспект» ситуации.

collocationTask.prompt: The crisis also has an important economic ___.
collocationTask.explanationRu: Экономическая сторона, аспект кризиса — an economic dimension. Deadline (срок), budget (бюджет) и balance (баланс) по смыслу не подходят.

nuance.text: Winning the lottery gave her financial freedom, but it also added a whole new [[dimension]] to her family problems.
nuance.explanationRu: Dimension хорошо сочетается с new/added: a whole new dimension. Aspect так почти не говорят — для него обычнее просто another aspect.

reverse.text: Let's look at the financial [[aspect]] of the deal before deciding.
reverse.explanationRu: Один конкретный аспект вопроса — просто aspect. Dimension обычно про более широкий, часто неожиданный оттенок ситуации, здесь это было бы слишком громко.

fixIt.text: The therapist's report added a completely new [[direction]] to the case, one nobody had expected.
fixIt.explanationRu: Direction — «направление» (куда двигаться), а не «сторона проблемы». Новую сторону, аспект ситуации — a new dimension.

wordFormation.text: Doctors now use three-[[dimensional]] scans to study the brain in more detail.

rewrite.original: The scandal wasn't only about money — it was also political.
rewrite.frame: The scandal had a political ____ as well as a financial one.

definitionEn: to make something seem smaller, weaker or less important than before
situation: Something makes a person's success, feelings or importance seem smaller than they really are.

examples.text: Nothing can [[diminish]] the courage she showed that night.
His influence in the party has steadily [[diminished]] since the scandal.
Regular exercise won't cure the illness, but it can [[diminish]] some of the symptoms.

texts: Losing this match won't [[diminish]] the team's achievement this season.
Time may [[diminish]] the pain, but the memory will stay.
Critics say the reform will [[diminish]] workers' rights.

badCollocation.text: Please [[diminish]] the volume on the TV.
badCollocation.noteRu: Громкость уменьшают глаголом lower или turn down: turn down the volume. Diminish — про значимость, влияние, размер в переносном смысле, а не про ручку громкости.

collocationTask.prompt: Losing the final doesn't ___ what the team achieved this year.
collocationTask.explanationRu: «Не умаляет достижение» — doesn't diminish the achievement. Shrink, lower и drop с achievement так не сочетаются.

nuance.text: No amount of criticism could [[diminish]] her pride in what she had built.
nuance.explanationRu: Diminish — умалить значение, гордость, ценность чего-то, звучит эмоционально. Reduce — обычно про количество, цифры (reduce costs), к гордости не подходит.

reverse.text: The company managed to [[reduce]] its costs by twenty percent.
reverse.explanationRu: Сокращение конкретных цифр, расходов — reduce. Diminish здесь звучало бы слишком книжно и не подходит к процентам.

fixIt.text: Losing the final doesn't [[decrease]] everything the team achieved this season.
fixIt.explanationRu: Decrease обычно про измеримые величины (decrease sales, decrease temperature). Умалить чьи-то заслуги — diminish.

wordFormation.text: Critics warned of a serious [[diminution]] of civil liberties under the new law.

reply.context: A colleague says: "I heard the new intern is being credited for the whole project now."
options: That's a shame — crediting only her really does diminish what the rest of the team did.
Relax, a good bonus like that always diminishes everyone's motivation.
OMG that is literally the single most devastating thing that has ever happened at this company!!
reply.explanationRu: Diminish — умалять чьи-то заслуги, здесь это уместно. Бонус обычно усиливает, а не diminishes motivation — второй вариант использует слово неверно. Третий — слишком эмоционально для рабочего разговора.

definitionEn: to fall or decrease slightly for a short time
senseNote: Базовое значение — физически окунуть что-то в жидкость (dip bread in soup). Здесь — переносное: показатель ненадолго немного снижается (temperatures dipped, sales dipped).
situation: A number such as a price, temperature, rating or level goes down a little before rising again.

examples.text: Sales usually [[dip]] in January after the busy holiday season.
The president's approval ratings [[dipped]] slightly after the tax announcement.
Temperatures will [[dip]] below freezing tonight, so take extra blankets.

texts: Consumer confidence tends to [[dip]] during uncertain times.
The pound could [[dip]] further if the talks collapse.
Attendance always seems to [[dip]] in the last week of term.

badCollocation.text: Profits [[dipped]] to a record low last year.
badCollocation.noteRu: Dip — про небольшое, обычно временное снижение. Если падение сильное и рекордное, говорят plunged или fell to a record low, а не dipped.

collocationTask.prompt: Share prices ___ briefly before recovering later in the day.
collocationTask.explanationRu: Dip — краткое, небольшое снижение с восстановлением. Collapsed (рухнули), vanished (исчезли) и exploded (резко выросли) с «briefly before recovering» не сочетаются.

nuance.text: The temperature will [[dip]] a little tonight, nothing too dramatic.
nuance.explanationRu: Dip — небольшое, некритичное снижение. Plunge — резкое, сильное падение; здесь прямо сказано «nothing too dramatic», поэтому plunge не подходит.

reverse.text: Shares [[plunged]] more than 30% after the scandal broke.
reverse.explanationRu: Падение больше чем на 30% — это plunge (резкое, сильное), а не лёгкое dip.

fixIt.text: Sales usually [[collapse]] a little in January before picking up again in February.
fixIt.explanationRu: Collapse — полный крах, после которого не «приходят в норму» через месяц. Небольшое, временное снижение — dip.

definitionEn: someone who is good at dealing with people and difficult situations without upsetting anyone
senseNote: Базовое значение — дипломат как профессия (представитель страны на переговорах). Здесь — переносное употребление: человек, который умеет ладить с людьми и решать деликатные ситуации, не обижая никого.
situation: Someone handles disagreements, complaints or sensitive situations so calmly and tactfully that nobody gets upset.

examples.text: You'll need to be a real [[diplomat]] to keep both families happy at the wedding.
As office manager, she has to be a [[diplomat]] when two team members disagree.
My father was always the [[diplomat]] of the family, smoothing over every argument.

texts: She's a natural [[diplomat]], even in the most awkward family gatherings.
You need to be a bit of a [[diplomat]] in this job.
Being the youngest in a big family taught him to be a [[diplomat]].

badCollocation.text: He's such a good [[diplomat]] at football.
badCollocation.noteRu: В переносном значении diplomat — про умение улаживать споры между людьми, а не про мастерство в спорте. Здесь лучше подойдёт skilled или talented player.

collocationTask.prompt: You'll have to be a real ___ to get both sides to agree.
collocationTask.explanationRu: Тактичного человека, который мирит стороны, называют a diplomat. Scientist, historian и electrician с этой ролью не связаны.

nuance.text: When her in-laws argue, she becomes a real [[diplomat]], calming everyone down without taking sides.
nuance.explanationRu: Diplomat (перен.) — про такт и умение мирить людей. Politician — про профессию или манипулятивное поведение ради выгоды, к семейным спорам не подходит.

reverse.text: As a local [[politician]], she has to answer difficult questions from journalists every week.
reverse.explanationRu: Здесь речь о профессии, связанной с выборами и властью, — politician. Diplomat подразумевает такт и умение мирить, а не публичную должность.

fixIt.text: Our new team leader is a real [[dictator]] when it comes to solving arguments between colleagues fairly.
fixIt.explanationRu: Dictator — тот, кто жёстко подавляет других. Тот, кто тактично улаживает споры, не обижая никого, — diplomat.

wordFormation.text: Years of careful [[diplomacy]] finally ended the border dispute.

reply.context: A friend asks: "How do you manage to stay friends with both of them after their breakup?"
options: Honestly, I just try to be a diplomat and never take sides.
I don't know, I guess I've always been such a diplomat that I never even talk to either of them anymore.
Dunno, guess I just don't care enough to pick sides tbh.
reply.explanationRu: Diplomat (перен.) — тот, кто тактично ведёт себя с обеими сторонами. Во втором ответе слово употреблено неверно: избегать общения — не то же самое, что мирить людей. Третий звучит слишком небрежно.

definitionEn: careful and tactful, so as not to upset or offend other people
senseNote: Другое значение — «относящийся к дипломатии, международным отношениям» (diplomatic relations, diplomatic immunity). Здесь — про тактичное поведение в общении, чтобы никого не обидеть.
situation: Someone chooses their words carefully in a difficult conversation so as not to upset or offend anyone.

examples.text: I tried to be [[diplomatic]] when my sister asked if I liked her new haircut.
The manager gave [[diplomatic]] feedback so the intern wouldn't feel discouraged.
It's hard to stay [[diplomatic]] when a client is clearly wrong but very senior.

texts: Try to be [[diplomatic]] — she worked really hard on this.
He gave a [[diplomatic]] answer that avoided taking sides.
It wasn't easy to stay [[diplomatic]] during the argument.

badCollocation.text: Try to be more [[diplomatic]] with your dog when it misbehaves.
badCollocation.noteRu: Diplomatic — про такт в общении с людьми, где важны чувства и мнения. К животным это слово обычно не применяют; тут подойдёт patient или gentle.

collocationTask.prompt: She gave a very ___ answer, avoiding the question without offending anyone.
collocationTask.explanationRu: Тактичный, уклончивый ответ — a diplomatic answer. Automatic, dramatic и athletic по смыслу сюда не подходят, хотя и рифмуются с diplomatic.

nuance.text: Rather than say what he really thought, he gave a [[diplomatic]] reply about needing more time to decide.
nuance.explanationRu: Diplomatic — мягкий, уклончивый ответ, чтобы никого не задеть. Honest подразумевал бы прямоту, а тут человек как раз избегает прямого ответа.

reverse.text: I'd rather you were completely [[honest]] with me, even if it hurts.
reverse.explanationRu: Здесь просят прямоты, а не мягкости — honest. Diplomatic скорее про уклончивую вежливость, что противоречит просьбе.

fixIt.text: He was very [[frank]] when he broke the bad news, choosing every word carefully so she wouldn't feel like a failure.
fixIt.explanationRu: Frank — прямой, откровенный, без обиняков. Здесь герой явно подбирает слова осторожно — это diplomatic, а не frank.

reply.context: A friend asks: "Be honest — do you think my business idea is any good?"
options: I'll be diplomatic: I love your enthusiasm, but I have a few concerns about the plan.
I'll be diplomatic: it's honestly the worst idea I've ever heard in my life.
Nah, it's rubbish, don't even bother.
reply.explanationRu: Diplomatic — смягчить критику, не обижая. Во втором ответе слова противоречат самому diplomatic: это грубо, а не тактично. Третий — слишком резко для разговора с другом.

rewrite.original: She chose her words very carefully so as not to upset her boss.
rewrite.frame: She was very ____ so as not to upset her boss.

definitionEn: a place on a computer where a set of related files are grouped together
senseNote: Более широкое, повседневное значение — справочник, список имён и контактов (a telephone directory). Здесь — компьютерный термин: папка, в которой хранятся файлы.
situation: On a computer, related files are grouped together in a named folder that can contain other folders inside it.

examples.text: Save the file in the project's main [[directory]], not on the desktop.
The script searches every [[directory]] on the drive for old log files.
Each user has their own home [[directory]] on the shared server.

texts: Create a new [[directory]] before you start the download.
The photos are stored in a separate [[directory]].
You don't have permission to open that [[directory]].

badCollocation.text: Please attach the [[directory]] to your email.
badCollocation.noteRu: К письму нельзя приложить directory (папку) целиком, только отдельный file. Если нужно отправить папку, её сначала архивируют (a zipped folder).

collocationTask.prompt: All the images for the app are kept in a single ___.
collocationTask.explanationRu: Место для хранения связанных файлов — a directory (папка). Password, browser и license к хранению файлов не относятся.

nuance.text: Move the images into a separate [[directory]] so the project folder doesn't get messy.
nuance.explanationRu: Directory — папка, которая может содержать много файлов. File — отдельный файл, а не контейнер для других файлов.

reverse.text: Double-click the [[file]] to open the report in Word.
reverse.explanationRu: Открывают конкретный документ — a file. Directory — это папка, которая содержит файлы, а не сам документ.

fixIt.text: Please move that [[file]] to the shared drive — it contains hundreds of documents and takes forever to upload.
fixIt.explanationRu: «Содержит сотни документов» — так говорят про папку, a directory. Один файл (file) не может содержать сотни документов внутри себя.

definitionEn: extremely unsuccessful or bad, often causing serious problems
senseNote: Базовое значение (B1) — вызванный настоящей катастрофой (a disastrous flood/earthquake). Здесь — преувеличенное, повседневное употребление: про очень плохой, провальный результат (a disastrous meeting, a disastrous first date).
situation: A decision, event or performance turns out extremely badly, causing serious problems or embarrassment for everyone involved.

examples.text: The product launch was [[disastrous]]: the app crashed in front of every journalist in the room.
Their first date was [[disastrous]] — he spilled wine on her dress within five minutes.
The company's decision to cut customer support proved [[disastrous]] for its reputation.

texts: The trip was fun at first, then became [[disastrous]].
His speech was [[disastrous]] and cost him the election.
The picnic turned [[disastrous]] when it started to pour with rain.

badCollocation.text: The weather was a bit [[disastrous]] today, so I took an umbrella.
badCollocation.noteRu: Disastrous — очень сильное слово («полный провал»), с «a bit» не сочетается. Про немного плохую погоду скажите bad или unpleasant weather.

collocationTask.prompt: The evening turned out to be completely ___ — nothing went according to plan.
collocationTask.explanationRu: Полный провал вечера — disastrous. Punctual (пунктуальный), optional (необязательный) и fashionable (модный) по смыслу не подходят.

nuance.text: The wedding was [[disastrous]]: the caterer never showed up and the marquee blew away in the storm.
nuance.explanationRu: Disastrous — крайне, катастрофически плохо. Bad — просто «плохо», слишком слабое слово для ситуации, где не приехал кейтеринг и унесло шатёр.

reverse.text: The coffee here is pretty [[bad]], but at least it's cheap.
reverse.explanationRu: Просто невкусный кофе — это bad, не более того. Disastrous было бы огромным преувеличением для такой мелочи.

fixIt.text: The interview was [[unpleasant]], mostly because she got every single question wrong and started crying.
fixIt.explanationRu: Unpleasant — просто «неприятно», слишком мягко для полного провала (все ответы неверны, слёзы). Здесь нужно disastrous.

wordFormation.text: The flood had a [[disastrous]] effect on the local economy.

reply.context: A friend asks: "How did the work presentation go this morning?"
options: Honestly? Disastrous. The projector broke and I froze halfway through.
Disastrous! Everyone loved it and I got a huge round of applause.
It was a most disastrous affair, one I shall not soon recover from, I fear.
reply.explanationRu: Disastrous — полный провал; во втором варианте описание явно положительное, поэтому слово употреблено неверно. Третий звучит слишком театрально для разговора с другом.

rewrite.original: The picnic was ruined completely when a storm suddenly hit.
rewrite.frame: The picnic was ____ when a storm suddenly hit.
